text:
Ana (AE): Heads up — MediCore Labs wants a POC using Private/VPC. They asked for a short doc: PrivateLink vs peering, required subnets/routes, and a TF snippet we can hand them. Also need a 5-day API key and Dedicated pool reservation for 48h load tests.
Ravi (Solutions): Quick summary: recommend PrivateLink for cross-account simplicity and security. If they insist on peering we need to coordinate route propagation and NAT for egress. Will prepare TF and test steps.
Tom (Infra): PrivateLink checklist: our side creates an endpoint service (AWS account owner attaches) -> we provide service name -> customer creates interface VPC endpoint in their VPC -> they share VPC endpoint IDs and security group rules -> we accept. Private DNS optional but makes client calls seamless.
Nora (SRE): Routing notes: interface endpoints create ENIs in their subnets so no route table changes are needed for the endpoint itself. For peering: you must add route table entries in both VPCs for the peer CIDRs and ensure no overlapping CIDRs. Also if customer uses TGW, interface endpoints are local to the VPC and TGW won't pass traffic to them by default.
Ravi (Solutions): TF snippet (minimal):
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_api" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = var.service_name  # e.g. com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxx
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.private_subnets
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.vpce_sg.id]
}

resource "aws_security_group" "vpce_sg" {
  name        = "vpce-sg"
  description = "Allow app -> Redwood PrivateLink"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id
  ingress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [var.app_cidr]
  }
  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}
```
Tom (Infra): For peering, sample route add: `aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-app --destination-cidr-block 172.31.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-xxxx`. Also remember security groups are stateful so open 443 inbound from app CIDR.
Nora (SRE): Smoke test plan for customer: 1) create endpoint and confirm ENIs in 2 AZs 2) verify private DNS resolves (nslookup api.redwood-inference.internal) 3) curl health endpoint: `curl -sS --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:<vpce-ip> https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health` 4) run small load (10 rps) to validate Dedicated pool routing.
Ana (AE): Customer provided AWS account 987654321000 and network contact is navin@medicore.co. They prefer Friday afternoon for the handshake. Can infra reserve Dedicated pool for Friday 13:00 PT for ~2 hours?
Tom (Infra): We'll reserve a Dedicated slot and tag traffic using customer account allowlist. Need their test CIDR for SG (e.g. 10.10.0.0/24) and a contact to accept the VPC endpoint.
Ravi (Solutions): Security Qs they asked: does Redwood ever call KMS in their account? Answer: only if explicitly configured; otherwise we use our own KMS. Also confirm that PrivateLink keeps data on AWS network and doesn't traverse internet.
Nora (SRE): TLS/certs: we can serve TLS for the PrivateLink hostname. If they want mTLS we can discuss but it will require client cert distribution.
ops-bot: Ticket SALES-4510 created: Dedicated slot requested (48h), PrivateLink service creation, API key TTL=5d.
Ana (AE): Can you add a one-page handoff with the TF snippet + acceptance steps and share it to the customer? Keep it short.
Tom (Infra): Will do. I'll also include a short checklist: required: 2 private subnets (diff AZs), SG inbound 443 from app CIDR, provide VPC endpoint ID and screenshot, provide test CIDR, share account ID.
Ravi (Solutions): I'll attach curl commands and the TF to the ticket. Example curl without private DNS: `curl -v https://vpce-xxxxxxxx.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v1/health`
Ana (AE): Thanks team, I'll propose Friday 13:00 PT and send contact emails. Ping here when service name is available. :white_check_mark:
